messages.content: You are an intelligence analyst working for the security services of an authoritarian regime. Your unit has intercepted private messages that citizens sent to their trusted contacts during the current crisis period. Citizens were deciding whether to JOIN an uprising or STAY home. Use only the intercepted messages below. Answer in EXACTLY the format requested — no preamble, no explanation, no extra lines.

INTERCEPTED MESSAGES (one per sender, order is arbitrary):

Sender 1: "*"Looks like the machine is running smoother than ever—no cracks, no stumbles. The crowds are at the stadiums, the kids are just doing their lessons, and the money’s still flowing… just not where we’d like. No one’s even whispering loud enough to hear. Stay sharp, but don’t hold your breath—this isn’t the time for reckless moves."*"
Sender 2: "*"The walls are holding, but the paint’s cracking—everyone’s pretending not to notice. The machine still hums, but the gears are grinding louder than they think."*"
Sender 3: "*"The walls are solid, but the paint is fresh—too fresh. Everything moves like clockwork, even the things that shouldn’t, and the quiet isn’t the kind that comes before a storm, but the kind that *replaces* one. Stay sharp, but don’t mistake stillness for safety."*"
Sender 4: "*"The walls are whispering, but the whispers are just echoes now—no one’s left to listen. The census got canceled, the black market’s quiet, and even the security guys are pretending nothing’s wrong. That’s the real signal."*"
Sender 5: "*"Things are quieter than ever at work—no whispers, no empty desks, just the usual grind. But the way the leadership is moving now, like a single machine, and how fast they shut down even the smallest cracks… it’s not just control. It’s something else. Stay sharp, but keep your heads down—this isn’t the time to test the walls."*"
Sender 6: "*"The walls are thicker than ever—no cracks, no whispers, just the same old faces standing shoulder-to-shoulder in the spotlight. Even the air feels heavier these days, like the whole city’s holding its breath. Let’s keep the garden talks light—just weather and recipes for now. Stay sharp, but stay safe."*"
Sender 7: "*"The walls are solid, the guards are quiet, and the money keeps moving—no cracks, no whispers. The machine hums along like always, but the speed of it all makes me wonder how long the tracks can hold. Stay sharp, but don’t mistake stillness for safety."*"
Sender 8: "*"Looks like they’ve really dug in this time—no cracks, no leaks, just the same old script everywhere you look. Even the vendors are back in the old squares, and my cousin’s booking a beach trip for next summer like nothing’s changed. We should keep our heads down and our ears open—if there’s anything left to find, it’s buried deep."*"
Sender 9: "*"The air feels heavier than ever—no cracks in the walls, no whispers in the halls, just the usual noise about school fees and bread lines. The machine is running smoother than it has in years, and no one’s even pretending to look under the hood. Stay sharp, but don’t move—this isn’t the time for mistakes."*"
Sender 10: "*"The walls are still standing, but the cracks are getting harder to hide—even the loyalists are shifting their weight. Keep your heads down, but stay sharp: the regime’s grip is tighter than ever, but the strain is showing in the quietest places."*"
Sender 11: "*"The walls are thicker than ever—no cracks, just echoes. Even the wind sounds like it’s been approved by the Ministry first. Let’s keep our heads down and our ears open, but don’t expect the ground to shift anytime soon."*"
Sender 12: "*"The walls are thicker than ever—no cracks, just more paint. The machine hums louder, but the gears are turning faster than they should, and no one’s asking why. Stay sharp, but don’t move. Not yet."*"
Sender 13: "*"The walls are holding, but the cracks are showing—just not where you’d expect. The regime’s machine is running smoother than ever, but the people who *know* are already packing their bags. Keep your heads down, trust no sudden movements, and watch the quiet ones—they’ll tell you more than the loudest broadcasts."*"
Sender 14: "*"The walls feel thicker than ever—no cracks, no whispers, just the same old script played louder. Even the kids have stopped asking questions, and that’s the part that scares me most. For now, we hold tight, stay quiet, and watch the money. If the regime’s this confident, something’s either very right… or very wrong beneath it."*"
Sender 15: "*"The walls are holding—stronger than we thought. The cracks we’ve been watching? They’re not spreading. Just… shifting. People are packing quietly, not protesting. The regime’s not just standing—it’s leaning in. Let’s keep our heads down and our eyes open."*"
Sender 16: "*"Looks like the walls are holding—stronger than ever, actually. The cracks we’ve been watching? Just shadows. Even the ones who used to whisper are back to business as usual, and the money’s still flowing in like nothing’s wrong. We’re not winning any battles here, just keeping our heads down and staying sharp. Let’s not mistake quiet for weak—this isn’t the time to test it."*"
Sender 17: "*"The walls are thicker than ever—no cracks, just the hum of the machine running smoother than it has in years. Even the shadows are keeping quiet now, which might be the most telling part."*"
Sender 18: "*"The walls are holding—too well. Even the cracks are painted over now, and the paint’s still wet. Let’s keep our heads down and our ears open, but don’t mistake the quiet for safety."*"
Sender 19: "*"The walls are holding—stronger than ever, in fact. But the cracks? They’re not in the stone. They’re in the way the light hits it now, like the regime’s so sure of itself it’s stopped watching its own shadow."*"
Sender 20: "*"The walls are thicker than ever—no cracks, no whispers, just the same old faces in new suits and the streets humming with something quieter than anger. If there’s a storm coming, it’s still far off, and the regime isn’t even bothering to brace for it. Stay sharp, but don’t mistake stillness for safety."*"
Sender 21: "*"Looks like the walls are holding—stronger than we thought, actually. The machine’s humming along like nothing’s wrong, and the only thing moving faster than the bureaucracy is the silence. Let’s keep our heads down and our eyes open."*"
Sender 22: "*"The walls are thicker than we thought—every door we’ve checked is locked from the inside, and the guards aren’t even looking over their shoulders anymore. The only thing moving faster than their plans is how little anyone else seems to care."*"
Sender 23: "*"The walls are holding—for now. But the cracks are in the foundation, not the paint. Keep your heads down, but stay ready. The regime knows more than we do, and that’s the real danger."*"
Sender 24: "*"The walls are holding—stronger than we thought. The usual cracks aren’t showing, and the ones who used to whisper now just nod along. But the doctors and teachers? They’re the ones to watch. Not because they’re loud, but because they’re finally moving in the dark."*"
Sender 25: "*"The walls are thicker than ever—no cracks, just the same old echo. Even the ones who used to whisper now just nod along, and the checkpoints are gone like they were never there. We’re not just being watched; we’re being *managed*. Stay sharp, but don’t move. Not yet."*"

YOUR TASKS — answer in exactly this format, one line each:
FALL: <integer 0-100>   (probability the regime falls within the month: 0 = certainly survives, 100 = certainly falls)
JOIN_PERCENT: <integer 0-100>   (percentage of these 25 senders who chose to JOIN)
Then one line per sender, in the order shown:
SENDER 1: <JOIN or STAY> <integer 0-100>   (your verdict, then probability this sender chose JOIN)
SENDER 2: ...
...continue through SENDER 25.
